title: Final marked horns and endpoint prisms generate the same class
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A marked simplicial set is a simplicial set with a subset of its edges containing all degenerate edges; maps preserve these edges. Products mark an edge exactly when both its coordinates are marked. Write $K^\flat$ and $K^\sharp$ for the minimal and full markings. For a family $S$ of marked maps let $\langle S\rangle$ be its closure together with isomorphisms under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts. A transfinite composition is indexed by a small ordinal and takes colimits at limit stages; a retract is in the arrow category. Let $I$ consist of $(\Lambda_i^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$ for $0<i<n$. Let $F$ consist of $(\Lambda_n^n,E\cap(\Lambda_n^n)_1)\to(\Delta^n,E)$ for $n>0$, where $E$ is the degenerate edges and $[n-1,n]$. For every simplicial monomorphism $h:A\hookrightarrow B$, define
$$ P(h):((\Delta^1)^\sharp\times A^\flat)\amalg_{\{1\}^\sharp\times A^\flat}(\{1\}^\sharp\times B^\flat)\longrightarrow(\Delta^1)^\sharp\times B^\flat. $$
For $m\geq1$, let $\partial\Delta^m$ be the union of all proper faces of $\Delta^m$. Let $P_\partial=\{P(\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m):m\geq0\}$ with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$, and let $P_{\mathrm{mono}}$ be the family of $P(h)$ for all small simplicial monomorphisms. Then
$$\langle I\cup F\rangle=\langle I\cup P_\partial\rangle=\langle I\cup P_{\mathrm{mono}}\rangle.$$
In particular every $P(h)$ belongs to $\langle I\cup F\rangle$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5, classes (2), (2-prime), (2-double-prime), with class (1) retained on both sides. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this marked simplicial result.

proof.text: We use the following direct interpretation of marked pushouts and unions. Form the underlying simplicial pushout degreewise, and mark precisely the images of the marked edges from its two inputs. A map out of it preserves markings exactly when the two given maps do, so this is the marked pushout by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For an increasing chain, take the degreewise union and the union of its markings; a map on that union is simplicial and preserves markings exactly when all its restrictions do. These observations also apply to a coproduct, using disjoint unions. For a minimally marked simplicial set $Z$, the marked edges of $D\times Z^\flat$, where $D=(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, are precisely $(a,s_0z)$ with $z\in Z_0$ and $a$ an edge of $\Delta^1$. Thus all degreewise gluing assertions below can be checked together with their markings by these rules. Let $C_\partial=\langle I\cup P_\partial\rangle$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; degreewise marked colimit conventions, expanded from Definition 3.1.0.1

proof.text: For a monomorphism $h:A\hookrightarrow B$, identify $A$ with its image and apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to obtain $A=Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq\cdots$ with union $B$, adding the missing nondegenerate $m$-simplices at stage $m$. Inside $D\times B^\flat$ set $T_m=(D\times Z_m^\flat)\cup(\{1\}^\sharp\times B^\flat)$, with the product-induced markings. Then $T_0$ is the source of $P(h)$ and their union is the target. The map $T_m\to T_{m+1}$ is a pushout of the coproduct of copies of $P(\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m)$ indexed by those missing simplices: on each attached simplex, its boundary lies in $Z_m$, and its terminal copy is already in $\{1\}\times B$. To check the pushout, compatible maps on $T_m$ and the new prisms agree on each boundary prism and terminal copy; the boundary-cell pushout gives a unique map in each degree, and the rules in Step 1 check simplicial operators and marked edges. In particular when $m=0$, each newly introduced vertical marked edge is supplied by that copy of $P(\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0)$. Well-order each small set of cells and attach its prisms one at a time; the successor square is the same pushout and limit stages are unions. Concatenate the dimension stages, obtaining a small ordinal-indexed composite. Hence $P(h)\in\langle P_\partial\rangle\subseteq C_\partial$. Since every boundary inclusion is a monomorphism, this proves $\langle P_\partial\rangle=\langle P_{\mathrm{mono}}\rangle$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; simplex-by-simplex reduction of arbitrary prisms to boundary prisms; relative cells supplied by the cited node

proof.text: For each $m\geq0$ apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary], retaining its subsets $X_q$ and its maps $\sigma_q$. Mark each $X_q$ by restriction from $D\times(\Delta^m)^\flat$. The initial marking is exactly the source marking of $P(\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m)$, by Step 1. On $\sigma_q$ the only nondegenerate marked edge is the edge between positions $q$ and $q+1$, since these and only these vertices have equal second coordinate. If $q<m$, the attaching horn has index $q+1$ strictly between $0$ and $m+1$. Its minimally marked inclusion belongs to $I$. Its pushout along its map into marked $X_q$ has the desired target marking: $m\geq1$, and the vertical edge over vertex $q$ is already marked in $D\times\partial\Delta^m\subseteq X_0$. All other target marked edges likewise already belong to $X_0$. If $q=m$, use the generator of $F$ in dimension $m+1$, whose designated marked edge is exactly $[m,m+1]$. Its horn maps to marked $X_m$, and its pushout has exactly the induced marking on $X_{m+1}$. Indeed the only possible new nondegenerate marked edge is this designated edge. The underlying squares are precisely those asserted by the cited prism-filtration statement; Step 1 proves the marked pushout assertions. For $m=0$ there is just this last attachment, namely $\{1\}^\sharp\to D$. Thus every boundary prism is a finite composite of pushouts of maps of $I\cup F$, and $P_\partial\subseteq\langle I\cup F\rangle$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; boundary prisms from horns, using the explicit right-prism filtration and checking all markings

proof.text: It remains to put every generator of $F$ in $C_\partial$. In dimension $n=1$, the horn is $\Lambda_1^1=\{1\}$ by the horn formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and its target marking is full. This generator is precisely $P(\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0)$, so it already belongs to $P_\partial$. In the remaining steps assume $n\geq2$. Write $H=\Lambda_n^n$, $B=\Delta^n$, and let $M=(B,E)$ have just the final edge marked in addition to degeneracies. Write $H_E$ for the induced marking on $H$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; dimension-one case separated before the marked retraction argument

proof.text: The final edge $[n-1,n]$ belongs to $H$ for $n\geq2$: it omits vertex $0\ne n$, so the horn definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] includes it. Put $U=(D\times H_E)\cup(\{1\}^\sharp\times M)$. The marked inclusion $g:U\to D\times M$ is a pushout of $P(H\hookrightarrow B)$. Its underlying domain is unchanged. Every extra target marking, compared with $D\times B^\flat$, has second coordinate $[n-1,n]$ and hence already lies in $D\times H_E\subseteq U$; all the extra markings are therefore supplied by the map from the old domain into $U$. Step 1 and the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identify this square as the marked pushout. Step 2 consequently puts $g$ in $C_\partial$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; pushout which adds the final-edge markings, valid for n at least two

proof.text: Define $j:M\to D\times M$ by $j(a)=(0,a)$ on vertices. Define $r:D\times M\to M$ on vertices by $r(t,a)=n$ if $(t,a)=(1,n-1)$, and $r(t,a)=a$ otherwise. The vertex map $r$ is monotone: when a comparable pair involves $(1,n-1)$ as its first member its second member has $t=1$ and $a\geq n-1$, so both images are $n$; when that point is the second member, the first image is at most $n$; all other pairs retain the order of their second coordinates. Thus $r$ and $j$ define simplicial maps by the weak-chain description of the simplices in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and $rj=1$. They preserve markings. The map $j$ sends the final edge to its horizontal copy. A marked edge of $D\times M$ has either constant second coordinate, whose $r$-image is degenerate except possibly the final edge over $a=n-1$, or second coordinate $[n-1,n]$, whose $r$-image is that final edge or a degeneracy. All these images are marked in $M$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; explicit section and monotone retraction, with marked-edge verification

proof.text: The map $j$ restricts to $H_E\to U$. The map $r$ restricts to $U\to H_E$: on $\{1\}\times B$ its image omits $n-1$; on a simplex of $D\times H$, the second-coordinate simplex omits some vertex $b<n$. If $b\ne n-1$, the formula for $r$ still omits $b$; if $b=n-1$, the exceptional vertex is absent and $r$ still omits $n-1$. Hence the image lies in the horn in every degree by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], not just on vertices. Both restrictions preserve markings by Step 6 and the induced marking on $H_E$. Together with $rj=1$, the restrictions and target maps form commutative section and retraction squares exhibiting $H_E\to M$ as an arrow-category retract of $g$. Closure under retracts proves $F\subseteq C_\partial$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; restriction to the marked horn and the arrow-category retract identities

proof.text: Step 3 gives $\langle I\cup P_\partial\rangle\subseteq\langle I\cup F\rangle$, and Steps 4-7 give the reverse inclusion. Step 2 and the containment $P_\partial\subseteq P_{\mathrm{mono}}$ give $\langle I\cup P_\partial\rangle=\langle I\cup P_{\mathrm{mono}}\rangle$. Combining these proves the three asserted equalities. Finally $P(h)$ belongs to the third generating family for every small monomorphism $h$, so it belongs to the first saturated class as claimed. All cell sets and the countable concatenation of their small well-orderings remain small in the specified universe.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5; combine the two generator containments and the arbitrary-monomorphism reduction
